topic: sallyport: A Mac Vault Running Authenticated Agent Actions over MCP

key_points: Free Mac app that holds API/SSH credentials in an encrypted local vault and executes authenticated actions for AI agents over MCP
Core inversion: the agent gets the operation, never the key — key never appears in the agent's environment, no reveal or export route
Fixed decision ladder trust model: vault gate -> per-call approval -> session gate -> observe; no policy language to misconfigure
Secure Enclave + Touch ID gate the vault; write-blind signed journal with hash chain audit
Channels: http.request, ssh.exec, and proxied remote/local MCP servers; seals and refreshes OAuth 2.1 tokens
Install: brew install --cask olegsotnikov/tap/sallyport; ~2 min to first gated call; Apple Silicon + macOS 14+; Apache-2.0, no account, no cloud, no telemetry
1Password Environments MCP Server: secrets injected at runtime for an authorized process; MCP server returns names, not values
Credentials stay out of model context; users must explicitly authorize scoped access
Available macOS and Linux; now on Cursor Marketplace; also trusted access layer for OpenAI Codex
Approach keeps credentials in a cloud-backed vault; agent acts without seeing secret values
Credential isolation for AI agents via placeholder tokens: agents get useless placeholder values, real keys injected at the network layer via a proxy
Structural guarantee (not policy) — the real key never enters agent memory, logs, or LLM context
Open-source; CLI with vault serve proxy and MCP stdio server; works with Claude Code / Cursor via 'wardn setup'
Proxy approach vs sallyport's executor approach
Local-first secret manager for the AI-agent era; keeps API keys out of .env and out of agent transcripts
Master password + TUI; rapg run -- injects env-tagged secrets into child processes; transcript redaction with pbpaste
Emphasizes keeping secrets off disk/scrollback rather than running actions on the agent's behalf
Zero-knowledge inject approach to keep API keys/tokens out of Claude Code's context window
GitGuardian 'State of Secrets Sprawl 2026' (Mar 17, 2026): 28.65M secrets in public repos, AI-assisted commits 3.2% leak rate
MCP server injects secret into a 0600 session file that the tool then sources; values never enter conversation
Practical tutorial framing for Claude Code secrets management
Arcade.dev acts as a secure cloud action runtime between Claude Code and the tools it calls
Vaults tool credentials centrally, eliminates local .env / raw tokens; executes with account permissions at the moment of use
Focus on execution-time authorization and reduced exfiltration risk vs a static token

stats.fact: Sallyport is written mainly in Swift (stack: Swift, Go, MCP); Apache-2.0 public core with no account, cloud service, or telemetry — runs entirely on the Mac.
First release 2026-07-14; 201 GitHub stars, 6 forks, topics include ai-agents, credentials, mcp, secrets-management, security (data as of 2026-09-11 update).
Sallyport requires Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 14 or newer; Intel Macs unsupported.
Install to first gated call takes about two minutes via Homebrew: brew install --cask olegsotnikov/tap/sallyport.
GitGuardian 'State of Secrets Sprawl 2026' (Mar 2026): 28.65 million secrets exposed in public repositories, with AI-assisted commits showing a 3.2% leak rate.

GitGuardian 2026: 28.6M new secrets exposed in public GitHub commits in 2025; 24,008 unique credentials surfaced inside MCP config files (claude_desktop_config.json, .cursor/settings.json); Google API keys ~20% of MCP leaks, PostgreSQL connection strings ~14%; 2,117 still valid.
Sallyport's cited risk context: 84 malicious package versions in a single npm attack that hunted credentials (Nx S1ngularity).

Anthropic shipped MCP tunnels (May 19, 2026) so credentials no longer have to ride inside the agent's context — a structural fix for the MCP credential problem, validating the 'keep the key out of the agent' model.
MCP spec mandates OAuth 2.1 with mandatory PKCE, Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591), Resource Indicators (RFC 8707), Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728), and CIMD for authentication.

angles: The core inversion: give the agent an operation, not a key — why 'the workload itself is untrusted' breaks traditional secret managers that hand the secret to the workload
Mac-only, on-device, Touch ID + Secure Enclave — a local-first alternative to cloud vaults (1Password) and proxy-based open source tools (wardn)
Concrete setup path: brew install, create vault, add credential, point any MCP client (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) at the 'sp mcp' gate
The fixed decision ladder (vault gate -> per-call approval -> session gate -> observe) as a no-policy-language security model that sidesteps misconfiguration
The 2026 MCP-credential moment: GitGuardian leak data, Anthropic MCP tunnels, and why secrets must stay out of agent context
Residual risk and honest boundaries: executor results may contain sensitive data, no credential-reveal/export route means reissue on vault loss
